headline: Checks before the road, or after it
reading: Two schedules for a new car on one time axis. United States: the maker designs, builds and certifies the car itself, it goes on the road, and the authority's tests and recalls come afterwards. Germany and the EU: an approval authority approves the type first, then the car is built and goes on the road. Once a type is approved, every car built to it goes on the road without its own approval; a car outside the approved type needs its own individual approval, the long way.

words.beyond: a car outside the approved type: its own approval, the long way

schedule.note: Schematic lengths in arbitrary units on one shared axis: the order and the relative length matter, no duration is measured. Building has the same length on both sides. The long approval stands for a vehicle approved on its own, outside an approved type (EU-2018-858), and on the company side for the period before 2021 (about six weeks per system, R11-12) and for a system beyond the standing agreement (R11-12).

us.label: United States
us.fact: The maker certifies its own vehicles against the federal safety standards; NHTSA does not approve them before sale. NHTSA buys certified new cars, tests them, and pursues a recall when one does not comply.

de.label: Germany
de.fact: A vehicle may be placed on the market, registered or put into service only once its type is approved (in Germany by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt). Each car built to the type comes with a certificate of conformity; a single vehicle outside an approved type needs an individual approval.

notesWhy: Removed from the figure on 17 November 2026: readers found the italic notes under the axis heavy, and the article text says the same. Kept here so that nothing is lost.

notes.text: No works council; for this kind of decision the checks come afterwards, as court cases and state rules.
The approval: the works council is told while planning, has to agree if the system can monitor staff, and a privacy review approves it. Until 2021 about six weeks per system.
Since 2021 a standing agreement approves IT systems inside fixed rules: one that fits goes live after a quick check, one outside needs its own agreement.
